diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let us consider a simplified fictitious method where the DE transformation \eqref{eq:DE} is replaced by the identity transformation $\varphi(s)=s$ and $p_j(s)$ is a piecewise linear function with $p_j(s_i)=\delta_{ij}$.
$P_j(s_i)=0$ for $i<j$ and the matrix $(w_{ij})$ is lower triangular

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the fictitious method (identity transformation plus piecewise-linear 'hat' interpolation functions) 'is nothing but the implicit Euler method'. With the identity transformation the weights are w_ij = P_j(s_i) = integral from a to s_i of the hat function p_j, so P_j(s_i)=h for j<=i-2, P_{i-1}(s_i)=h/2... more precisely P_j(s_i)=h for j<i, P_i(s_i)=h/2, and P_j(s_i)=0 for j>i. Hence the scheme is x_i = x_a + h*sum_{j<i} f(t_j,x_j) + (h/2) f(t_i,x_i), whose increment is x_i - x_{i-1} = (h/2)(f(t_i,x_i)+f(t_{i-1},x_{i-1})). This is the implicit trapezoidal (Crank-Nicolson) rule, not the implicit Euler rule x_i - x_{i-1} = h f(t_i, x_i), which would require piecewise-constant (right-endpoint) interpolation. The identification, not the triangularity, is what fails.

failure_location.quote: In fact, this method is nothing but the implicit Euler method and the lower triangularity means that the method respects causality

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'the implicit Euler method' with 'the implicit trapezoidal rule (Crank-Nicolson method)' (or, to obtain implicit Euler, replace the piecewise linear p_j by a piecewise constant right-endpoint function). The lower-triangularity/causality argument and all other results are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Only the heuristic identification in the 'Intuitive explanation' subsection is wrong; the near-lower-triangularity claim, the causality argument, Theorems 3.1 and 3.2, and all numerical guarantees are unaffected.
issues.title: Fictitious hat-function method misidentified as the implicit Euler method
issues.why_classification: A single local wording/mathematical mislabeling in an intuitive-explanation remark; correcting the method name preserves every substantive claim, theorem, and guarantee, so the repair is short, local, and routine.
